answer: We formulate a mechanism combining dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices, inducing a strategic plume of identity verification costs that outweigh Sybil multiplication benefits. In this framework, agents optimizing expected payoffs navigate a sonnet of incentives discouraging identity duplicity. As agents iteratively update strategies, a spiral of diminishing Sybil returns emerges, guaranteeing strict Nash equilibrium convergence wherein honest participation dominates, rendering Sybil attacks unprofitable.
